name: Shanmugasundaram Selvam
profile: Long-time non-executive, non-independent director of Sun TV Network (on the board from 10 Aug 2009) and a major shareholder (67.7 lakh shares). Died suddenly on 10 October 2024, per Sun TV's FY2024-25 annual report.
notes: Deceased 10 Oct 2024. Source: Sun TV Network Annual Report 2024-25 (NSE), https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SUNTV1_28082025163743_Annual_Report_2024-25.pdf

name: Tu Jian
profile: Listed once on the Hurun China Rich List (2008) at about US$150m, with wealth attributed to 'Huaxinliuhe' (investments). Searches in English and Chinese (涂建 华信六合) found no profile, company page or news coverage confirming who he is or what he does now.
notes: Could not identify. 'Huaxinliuhe' may be a transliteration of a company name (e.g. 华信/华新 六合). Not the same person as Loncin's Tu Jianhua (涂建华). A Chinese company registry check would be needed. Low priority.

name: Matthew J. Missad
current_role: Executive Chairman, UFP Industries (Grand Rapids, MI); agreed to stay through 2026
profile: Career-long UFP Industries executive (wood/composite building, packaging and industrial products). He was EVP and general counsel from 1996, CEO from July 2011 to Dec 2024 and chairman from 2023. He became executive chairman when Will Schwartz took over as CEO at the start of fiscal 2025.
interesting_fact: Became UFP's fifth CEO in its history (July 2011) after more than 25 years at the company, much of it as its top lawyer.
deep_cut_fact: Started at UFP in 1978 as a high-school student working part-time on the maintenance crew. He paid his own way through college and law school, then joined full-time in 1985 as manager of legal compliance.
notes: Press contact (Lynn Afendoulis, Director of Corporate Communications) comes from a Feb 2023 release; check a recent UFP release to confirm it is current.

name: Scott H. Baxter
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Kontoor Brands (Wrangler, Lee, Helly Hansen); director at Lowe's
profile: Has led Kontoor Brands since August 2018, when it was spun out of VF Corp as the home of Wrangler and Lee. He has been chairman since 2021. Before VF (2007-2018, including group president roles over The North Face and Vans) he spent about 20 years at Nestle, PepsiCo and Home Depot, where he was SVP running the services division.
interesting_fact: Spent the first half of his career in suits at consumer and retail companies. He now wears denim to work and says he often gives away Wrangler and Lee clothes when someone compliments them: 'It shocks people, but 99% of the time, they take it.'
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate, he turned down a job offer from the US Secret Service to start his career at Nestle.
notes: Kontoor is based in Greensboro, NC. The Brunswick Review interview (2023) is a good source of rapport material.

name: G. Zachary (Zack) Gund
profile: Member of the Cleveland Gund family, longtime major Kellogg shareholders. He founded the private-capital firm Coppermine Capital in 2002 and still runs it. He was a Kellogg/Kellanova director from Dec 2014 and later lead independent director of the WK Kellogg Co spin-off. Both board seats likely ended when Ferrero bought WK Kellogg (2025) and Mars bought Kellanova.
interesting_fact: The Gund family and the Kellogg Foundation Trust agreed to vote 21.7% of WK Kellogg's stock in favour of Ferrero's US$3.1bn takeover of the cereal maker.
deep_cut_fact: Coppermine's portfolio includes B2U, which builds grid storage from second-life EV batteries, and Little Leaf Farms, a controlled-environment lettuce grower. These are useful hooks for an energy-focused podcast.
notes: His firm's website publishes his direct work email. The Kellogg board status after the 2025 acquisitions is not confirmed from a primary source. University of Vermont BA and Kellogg (Northwestern) MBA, per third-party databases.

name: Rahul Sharma
current_role: Co-founder, Micromax Informatics; drives its AI/semiconductor pivot (MiPhi Semiconductors JV with Taiwan's Phison) and Bhagwati Products
profile: Co-founded Micromax in 2000 with Vikas Jain, Sumit Arora and Rajesh Agarwal. It began as an IT/telecom hardware firm and became one of India's top phone brands after 2008. He founded electric-motorcycle maker Revolt Intellicorp (2019), which RattanIndia fully acquired in 2023. He now focuses on electronics components, AI storage chips (MiPhi) and a Rs 250 crore deeptech family office.
interesting_fact: Micromax's MiPhi joint venture with Taiwan's Phison designs and makes AI-enabled storage chips in India. In 2026 the family set up a Rs 250 crore family office to back deeptech startups.
deep_cut_fact: Micromax's first big hit came from a trip to a village with no grid power, where a phone booth ran on a truck battery that its owner cycled to the next village each night to charge. Sharma came back and built the X1i, a phone with a 30-day battery.
notes: Many Indians share this name; this record is the Micromax co-founder. I found no published press or IR email (the only email on MiPhi's site is customer care). The truck-battery story appears in many outlets (CNN Money 2016, Business Standard 2010, YourStory), though accounts disagree on whether the village was in West Bengal or Bihar. It fits an energy angle well.

name: Pramod Madhukar Chaudhari
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Praj Industries (Pune); Chairman, Praj HiPurity Systems
profile: IIT Bombay mechanical engineer (1971) who worked on the shop floor at Force Motors (Bajaj Tempo) and in technical sales at Widia before founding Praj in Pune in the mid-1980s (1983, 1984 and 1985 all appear in sources). Praj started as a supplier of ethanol plants and grew into India's leading biofuels and industrial-biotech engineering firm, with work in 2G ethanol, compressed biogas (CBG) and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).
interesting_fact: IIT Bombay calls Praj India's most successful biofuels company. Chaudhari has received the BioSpectrum Leadership Award for three decades of promoting biofuels and a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Sugar Technologists' Association of India.
deep_cut_fact: As an IIT Bombay student he joined a shramdaan (volunteer labour) effort that built a school near Patan in Satara district after the 1967 Koyna earthquake, which he calls his most cherished memory of the institute. He also endowed IITB's Chair Professorship for Green Chemistry and Industrial Biotechnology.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (ethanol, SAF, bio-energy). Praj publishes interviews with him on praj.net, which suggests he is media-friendly. info@praj.net is the general head-office address.

name: Joshua (Josh) Jergensen
current_role: President & Chief Operating Officer, PACS Group, Inc. (NYSE: PACS), Farmington, Utah
profile: Senior operator at PACS Group, a fast-growing US post-acute and skilled-nursing company (from 2 facilities in 2013 to 324). He has provided operational support across the PACS portfolio since 2014 and is now president and COO, driving acquisitions such as a 32-facility Florida deal. His wealth comes from PACS stock after the 2024 IPO.
interesting_fact: PACS grew from two facilities in 2013 to 324 within about a decade (roughly 16,000%), a story Jergensen presented at Utah Business's Forward event in 2026 under the theme 'healthcare is local'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed nursing home administrator and approved preceptor (trainer of new administrators) in California. He holds a BYU Marriott business degree and a USC master's in healthcare administration, and is a keen golfer.
notes: Not a co-founder (Jason Murray and Mark Hancock founded PACS). Healthcare operator with little link to energy or data centres.

name: Arnon Dinur
current_role: Partner, 83North (Israeli/European VC, formerly Greylock Israel); director, Via Transportation (NYSE: VIA)
profile: Israeli venture investor, partner at 83North, which led Via's US$110m round at a US$3.5bn valuation in 2023. He sits on Via's board, and his holding became public wealth after Via's IPO. Exits he was involved in include Wolt (DoorDash), Marqeta, SuperPlay (Playtika) and BlueVine. Current boards include Holidu, Podimo, Lendbuzz and Mixtiles.
interesting_fact: Before venture capital he worked at M-Systems, the Israeli company that invented the USB flash drive, and stayed on at SanDisk after its US$1.6bn acquisition of M-Systems.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Lobby99, a crowd-funded Israeli non-profit that lobbies the Knesset on behalf of the public interest rather than corporate clients.
notes: 83North publishes his work email (assistant: stacey@83north.com on the same page). VCs tend to welcome podcast invitations. Education details (law background, MBA from Texas McCombs) appear only on aggregator sites and are unverified.

name: Margaret (Margo) Hastings Georgiadis
current_role: Director, AppLovin and McDonald's; CEO-Partner, Flagship Pioneering; co-founder/CEO of Montai Therapeutics until its Nov 2026 merger into Valo Health, after which she was reported to become an adviser
profile: Veteran operator with a Harvard economics BA and MBA. She was a McKinsey partner, EVP/CMO at Discover, COO of Groupon, president of Google Americas, CEO of Mattel (2017-18) and CEO of Ancestry (2018-2020). At Flagship she co-founded Montai, an AI drug-discovery company. She has been on McDonald's board since about 2015 and AppLovin's since 2021.
interesting_fact: Her career spans consulting, credit cards, search, toys, consumer genomics and AI drug discovery: Google Americas president, Mattel CEO, Ancestry CEO, then founder of an AI-chemistry biotech.
deep_cut_fact: Montai's platform uses AI to decode 'nature's diverse chemistry' (compounds from foods and natural products) to design oral medicines. Its lead drug, MTAI-1025, is an oral STAT6 inhibitor for atopic dermatitis that now heads the merged Valo pipeline.
notes: Her role is in flux after the Valo-Montai merger (Nov 2026), so the montai.com press address may soon lapse. Flagship Pioneering's press office is an alternative route. She is commonly known as 'Margo'. Strong AI and tech angle (AppLovin).

name: Hilton H. Howell Jr.
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, Gray Media (NYSE: GTN), Atlanta; also Chairman/CEO of Atlantic American Corp
profile: Atlanta executive and lawyer who joined Gray's board in the 1990s after J. Mack Robinson's investor group took control. He became vice chairman in 2002 and CEO in 2008, when the stock had fallen to about 16 cents. He then led a run of acquisitions, including the US$3.65bn Raycom deal in 2018, that made Gray one of the largest US local-TV station owners.
interesting_fact: Under Howell, Gray bought the former GM Doraville assembly plant in 2021 to build 'Assembly Atlanta', a studio-city film and TV production campus, and also bought Third Rail Studios. It was an unusual move for a broadcaster.
deep_cut_fact: He took over as CEO in 2008, when Gray shares traded as low as 16 cents and the NYSE was warning about delisting. He then turned the over-leveraged regional group into the third-largest US TV station owner.
notes: The deep-cut fact touches on Gray's 2008 low point, so frame it as a turnaround story. Assembly Atlanta (studio campus on a former GM plant) is a good real-estate/infrastructure hook. Gray's press releases list executive contacts (CFO and an EVP) by phone; I found no published press email. Education per aggregators: Baylor, UT Austin MBA, Baylor Law (unverified). Web search budget ran out at this person, so contacts were not researched further.

name: Michael P. (Mike) Plisinski
current_role: CEO and director, Onto Innovation (NYSE: ONTO), Wilmington, MA
profile: Semiconductor process-control executive. He was CEO of Rudolph Technologies from Nov 2015 and has led Onto Innovation since Rudolph merged with Nanometrics in Oct 2019. Onto makes inspection, metrology and lithography tools used in advanced packaging for AI chips. He holds a UMass computer science BS and completed Harvard's Advanced Management Program.
interesting_fact: Onto's process-control and advanced-packaging tools sit in the AI chip supply chain (HBM and advanced packaging). In Nov 2026 the company expanded its buyback, citing confidence in the industry outlook.
deep_cut_fact: He was the sole founder and president of Counterpoint Solutions (1999-2003), a small optical review and automated metrology equipment start-up. It was acquired by August Technology, which Rudolph later bought, putting him on the path to CEO. He also sits on the board of Cognizer.AI.
notes: Good fit for the data-center/AI hardware angle. Sidney Ho is the investor contact on Onto's Nov 2026 press release. Board member of the Massachusetts High Technology Council.

name: Timothy M. Deane
current_role: Senior Vice President, Applied Global Services (AGS), Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT)
profile: Career Applied Materials executive who joined in 1995 and rose through field operations, account and region general manager roles and head of field operations for the Semiconductor Products Group. He has run Applied Global Services, the chip-equipment services, parts and upgrades business, since 2022 and was promoted to SVP in Dec 2024. His wealth comes from AMAT equity.
interesting_fact: In fiscal 2025 his AGS unit delivered record revenue of US$6.4bn. More than two-thirds came from long-term subscription service agreements (average contract about 2.9 years), with a backlog of about US$7.1bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Applied in 1995 in field operations and worked up through account and region general manager roles, about 30 years at one company, before taking over the services division.
notes: Low public profile, with few interviews. The best route is Applied Materials corporate communications. I found no published press or IR email in the time available (web search budget was exhausted). Relevant to AI chip-fab capacity.

name: Richard William (Rick) Svetkoff
current_role: Former founder/CEO/Executive Chairman of Starfighters Space, Inc. (NYSE American: FJET); resigned 19 Feb 2026; remains ~19% holder
profile: Founder and long-time leader of Starfighters (Kennedy Space Center, Florida), which flies the world's only commercial fleet of flight-ready Lockheed F-104 supersonic jets and is developing the 'StarLaunch' air-launch system for small payloads. He resigned all company roles in Feb 2026 but holds about 10.6m shares (~19%), the basis of his listed wealth.
interesting_fact: Starfighters operates the world's only commercial fleet of flight-ready F-104s, the first production aircraft to sustain Mach 2 in level flight and one NASA used for high-speed research. The company plans to use them to air-launch small rockets.
notes: CAUTION: a contested situation. He resigned in Feb 2026, and the company's 10-K and Nov 2026 proxy disclose litigation between him and Starfighters and allegations from an internal investigation. Not a good outreach target via the company. I found no published personal contact, and I did not record the home address that appears in SEC filings.

name: Kirk A. McLaughlin
current_role: Independent Director, National Bank Holdings Corp (NYSE: NBHC), since Jan 7, 2026
profile: West Texas community banker. He joined Vista Bank (Ralls, TX) in 1982, was its president from 1989 to 2018 and CEO from 2008 to 2015, and served 43 years on its board. He grew it from one branch in Ralls to 11 South Plains locations plus a Lubbock operations center. He joined NBHC's board when NBHC acquired Vista Bancshares in January 2026, and his large Vista stake turned into NBHC shares.
interesting_fact: Served two terms as Mayor of Ralls, Texas, and was a Class A director of the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas (1995-2000), chairing its audit committee from 1996.
deep_cut_fact: He was also a partner in Caprock Independent Insurance Agency for 20 years (1990-2010). He is a Texas Tech BBA who completed the ABA's National Agricultural Credit School, a sign of the farm-lending roots of a small-town South Plains bank.
notes: Low-profile regional banker (age 67) and a weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast, though the West Texas/Permian region is relevant. NBHC's media contact on press releases is dave.coons@nbhbank.com.

name: Randall W. (Randy) Edgar
current_role: CEO and Director, Suncrete, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMIX), Tulsa, Oklahoma
profile: Tulsa concrete entrepreneur, age 69. A former KPMG CPA, he was VP of Mid-Continent Concrete and then president under Mexican cement maker GCC after it bought the company (2006). He founded Eagle Redi-Mix Concrete in 2008, which grew into Suncrete, a ready-mix concrete platform across Oklahoma, Arkansas, Texas and Louisiana. Suncrete listed in 2026 through a SPAC merger led by Ned Fleming and Mark Matteson.
interesting_fact: Suncrete plans to roll up ready-mix producers across the US Sunbelt. Concrete is a key input for the region's data-centre, energy and infrastructure build-out, which makes him a good fit for the podcast's themes.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a CPA at KPMG before entering concrete. He holds an accounting degree from the University of Tulsa and founded his own company, Eagle Redi-Mix, in 2008 after running GCC's US ready-mix arm.

public_contacts.value: Dennard Lascar Investor Relations (Rick Black), suncrete@dennardlascar.com

notes: Newly public company, so management may be open to media. IR is handled by Dennard Lascar.

name: Jon M. Gibbs
current_role: Senior President, ExxonMobil Global Operations (since Jan 1, 2026); named executive officer of Exxon Mobil Corp
profile: ExxonMobil executive, age 54. He was SVP of Global Project Delivery (2020-21) and then president of ExxonMobil Global Projects Company (2021-2025), the unit that delivers Exxon's major capital projects. From January 2026 he runs the newly created Global Operations organisation and became one of five named executive officers in the 2026 proxy. His wealth comes largely from Exxon restricted stock.
interesting_fact: In 2025 he became one of ExxonMobil's five named executive officers alongside CEO Darren Woods. His unvested performance shares were valued at about US$42.7m at year-end 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before running all of Exxon's global operations, he spent five years running its Global Projects Company, the in-house organisation that builds the company's megaprojects (LNG, deepwater, chemicals).
notes: Highly relevant to energy (operations and megaprojects), but a low public profile. Approach through ExxonMobil media relations (corporate.exxonmobil.com newsroom). The web search budget ran out, so I could not research interviews or a more personal deep-cut fact.

name: Thomas M. Wynne
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer, Alliance Resource Partners LP (NASDAQ: ARLP), Tulsa, OK
profile: Career coal-mining engineer, age 69. He joined Alliance's predecessor in 1981 as a mining engineer, became VP of operations in 1998 and has been COO since March 2009, running the mines of one of the largest US thermal coal producers (Illinois Basin and Appalachia). His wealth comes from ARLP units.
interesting_fact: He has served the industry on the National Executive Committee for National Mine Rescue and is a past chairman of the Kentucky Coal Association. Alliance's coal supplies power plants that are now meeting rising data-centre electricity demand.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the company 45 years ago (1981) as a junior mining engineer, fresh from a Pitt mining engineering degree (later a WVU MBA), and worked his way up to COO.
notes: Strong energy/grid-reliability angle (coal for baseload power and data-centre demand). Mine safety and rescue is a good positive topic. CEO Joe Craft is the company's usual public voice.

name: George J. Still Jr.
current_role: Independent Director (Compensation Committee chair), Workday; Partner Emeritus, Norwest Venture Partners; founder, Still Capital Partners
profile: Silicon Valley venture capitalist, age 68. A Penn State accounting graduate and Tuck MBA, he worked at Ernst & Young and was a partner at Centennial Funds before joining Norwest Venture Partners in 1989, where he was co-managing partner from 1994 to 2014. He has been on Workday's board since 2009 (its longest-serving independent director) and runs his own firm, Still Capital Partners.
interesting_fact: He has been on Workday's board since 2009, three years before its IPO. As its longest-serving independent director he chairs the compensation committee.
deep_cut_fact: He led the only venture capital investment PeopleSoft ever took, and sat on its board from 1991 to 2001. PeopleSoft was Dave Duffield's company and the predecessor to Workday, which Duffield and Aneel Bhusri founded after Oracle's hostile takeover.
notes: Workday's contact addresses come from 2021-2022 releases; Norwest Venture Partners (nvp.com) is an alternative route. Good guest for founder and VC history (PeopleSoft to Workday).

name: Marion Brent Beason
profile: Reported as a holder of more than 5% (about 914k shares, 6.6%) of LendingTree (NASDAQ: TREE) in a Schedule 13G/A filed March 4, 2026, per LendingTree's 2026 proxy. The filing came on the same day as filings by the Estate of founder Doug Lebda, Lebda Family Holdings and others, which suggests he may hold the shares in a fiduciary or trustee role connected with the Lebda estate rather than as an operator. Not confirmed.
notes: Charlotte, NC-based. His role is unclear, and the holding is probably fiduciary, tied to the estate of LendingTree founder Doug Lebda (died 2025). The listed wealth may not be his own. Low priority and sensitive context; not recommended for outreach. The web search budget was exhausted before identity could be confirmed. I did not record the address from the filing.
